readout_other: Sensory-nerve conduction velocity (SNCV) and amplitude of evoked response (AER) of orthodromic sensory potentials of the median nerve
direction_notes: No significant differences in sensory-nerve conduction velocity or amplitude of evoked response were found between ultrasound (0.5, 1.0 or 1.5 W/cm2) and placebo (0.0 W/cm2) groups, or across intensities, after 10 minutes of treatment.

exposures.label: Therapeutic ultrasound applied to forearm overlying the median nerve

timing.protocol_description: After determining the pretest values, either ultrasound treatment of 0.5, 1.0, or 1.5 W/cm2 for 10 minutes or placebo ultrasound treatment of 0.0 W/cm2 for 10 minutes was applied to experimental and control subjects, respectively. The ultrasound was applied at a rate of about 6 cm/sec using a counterclockwise circular motion for a distance of 25 to 40 cm, depending on the length of the subject's mid forearm. Treatments were administered with minimal intervals of 48 hours.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound treatments were administered with a Rich-Mar VI Ultrasound unit† that had been calibrated just before the investigation and generated an average frequency of 1 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: After determining the pretest values, either ultrasound treatment of 0.5, 1.0, or 1.5 W/cm² for 10 minutes or placebo ultrasound treatment of 0.0 W/ cm² for 10 minutes was applied to experimental and control subjects, respectively.
source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirteen subjects were assigned to either Experimental or Control Groups for ultrasound or placebo treatments.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Intrasubject variability was reduced by repeating three ultrasound or three placebo treatments at each of the preselected intensity levels on the 13 subjects, rather than selecting three sets of 13 subjects each.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: Ultrasound treatments were administered with a Rich-Mar VI Ultrasound unit† that had been calibrated just before the investigation and generated an average frequency of 1 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: The purpose of this study was to contribute to the existing literature by specifically investigating the effect of three different ultrasound intensity levels (0.5, 1.0, 1.5 W/cm²) on the conduction velocity and amplitude of an evoked orthodromic sensory potential of the median nerve.

flags.reason: Paper reports only 'ultrasound intensity' in W/cm^2 (device moved over skin) without specifying ISPPA, ISPTA or SATA; recorded here as isppa_w_cm2 for schema compliance.
Paper does not state whether the Rich-Mar VI unit was operated in continuous or pulsed mode.

Classified as inactive_transducer because the control arm received 'placebo ultrasound treatment (0.0 W/cm2)', i.e. the same device/procedure with zero acoustic output; the paper gives no further detail of how the placebo was produced.
